title: Bounded tensor preparation for the boundary direct-image comparison
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\ge1$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], $l=i_e^*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and $C_W=\nu_W^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Let $r\le s$ and $u\le v$ be integers. Let $B\in D^b_c(Z_e,A)$ satisfy $\mathcal H^j(B)=0$ for $j\notin[r,s]$, and let $M\in D^b_c(T_e,A)$ have Tor amplitude $[u,v]$: for every degree-zero $A$-module sheaf $V$, $\mathcal H^j(M\otimes_A^LV)=0$ for $j\notin[u,v]$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].
There exist a complex $B^\bullet$ representing $B$, zero outside $[r,s]$, and a complex $V^\bullet$ representing $M$, with flat terms and zero outside $[u,v]$, such that $V^\bullet$ and its termwise pullback $lV^\bullet$ are K-flat and $lV^\bullet$ represents $lM$. Flat means that tensoring with a term is exact; K-flat means that total tensor with any acyclic complex is acyclic [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. The signed total complex
$$\operatorname{Tot}(B^\bullet\otimes_A lV^\bullet)^d=\bigoplus_{j+h=d}B^j\otimes_A lV^h,$$
with differential $d_B\otimes1+(-1)^j1\otimes d_{lV}$ on bidegree $(j,h)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], represents $Q=B\otimes_A^LlM$ and is zero outside $[r+u,s+v]$. Thus $Q\in D^b(Z_e,A)\subset D^+(Z_e,A)$ with precisely that cohomological bound. Its canonical direct-image mate
$$b_Q:C_TRi_{e,*}Q\longrightarrow Ri_{p,*}C_ZQ$$
of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] is defined and invertible. No finite Tor amplitude is required of $B$, and the flat terms of $V^\bullet$ are not asserted to be locally free. These assertions include $Z=\varnothing$, zero inputs and intervals with equal endpoints.

source.place: Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat; the etale finite-Tor flat-model clause of lem-sf-flat-model supplies the bounded input, followed by its tensor with a bounded representative.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-representative] to the abelian category of ordinary $A_Z$-module sheaves and the given cohomology vanishing of $B$, with $a=r,b=s$. It gives a complex $B^\bullet$, zero outside $[r,s]$, and an isomorphism $B\cong Q_Z(B^\bullet)$. Here $Q_W$ denotes localization of complexes on $W_{\Et}$. This step uses no Tor-amplitude hypothesis on $B$.

Use the small-etale-site clause of [lem-sf-flat-model], with $K=M,a=u,b=v$. The coefficient ring is exactly $A_{E,n}$, $\ell$ is invertible on $T$ because $\ell\ne p$, $M$ is bounded constructible, and $u\le v$. The asserted Tor amplitude is therefore condition (i) of that lemma. It supplies $V^\bullet$ representing $M$, zero outside $[u,v]$, whose terms are flat in the sense of that lemma: $V^h\otimes_A-$ preserves injections of $A_T$-module sheaves. Since $V^h\otimes_A-$ also preserves cokernels [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits], it carries short exact sequences to short exact sequences and is exact; composing with the symmetry $\mathcal G\otimes_AV^h\cong V^h\otimes_A\mathcal G$, the sheafification of the sectionwise symmetry of module tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], each $V^h$ is flat in the sense of [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the notion used below. This complex is bounded above by $v$, so [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes it K-flat. Only the flat-model equivalence is used, not its stronger constructible-model clause.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; bounded input: lem-sf-flat-model, etale clause

proof.text: For constant $A$ on the small etale sites, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies $i_e^*$ with the exact inverse image, using the canonical isomorphism $i_e^{-1}A_T\cong A_Z$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] shows that the termwise complex $lV^\bullet$ represents $lM$: explicitly apply the induced derived functor to $M\cong Q_T(V^\bullet)$ and then its displayed comparison with $Q_Z(lV^\bullet)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] to this morphism of constant-ring topoi and the flat-term K-flat complex $V^\bullet$. It says that $lV^\bullet$ is K-flat and has flat terms. Since the additive pullback carries zero to zero, it is still zero outside $[u,v]$.

Apply the right-factor version of [lem-trf-site-one-sided-tensor-normalization] on $(Z_{\Et},A_Z)$, with fixed flat-term K-flat factor $lV^\bullet$ and arbitrary complex $B^\bullet$. The resulting isomorphism, composed with those from steps 1 and 3, identifies $B\otimes_A^LlM$ with $Q_Z\operatorname{Tot}(B^\bullet\otimes_A lV^\bullet)$. The cited statement explicitly permits $B^\bullet$ to be non-flat and non-K-flat. By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the total terms are $\bigoplus_{j+h=d}B^j\otimes_A lV^h$ and the differential on bidegree $(j,h)$ is $d_B\otimes1+(-1)^j1\otimes d_{lV}$, exactly the complex in the statement.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor and its preceding construction, with right-factor normalization

proof.text: For a nonzero summand of the degree-$d$ total term one must have $r\le j\le s$, $u\le h\le v$, and $j+h=d$. These imply $r+u\le d\le s+v$. Thus every summand, and hence the total term, is zero if $d<r+u$ or $d>s+v$; only finitely many summands occur in any degree. The formula $\mathcal H^d=\ker(d^d)/\operatorname{im}(d^{d-1})$ from [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] then gives zero cohomology in those degrees. Consequently $Q=B\otimes_A^LlM$ belongs to $D^b(Z_e,A)$ and to $D^+(Z_e,A)$, with lower bound $r+u$ and upper bound $s+v$. This is a vanishing bound; it does not require nonzero cohomology at either endpoint.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor; elementary degree support of the direct-sum total complex

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], $i$ is proper. Unpacking [def-weil-proper-morphism] gives separatedness and finite type; unpacking [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives quasi-compactness. By [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated], the separated morphism $i$ is quasi-separated. These verify the geometric hypotheses of the direct-image comparison, independently of any cohomological amplitude.

The ring $A=A_{E,n}$ is finite by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], clause 4, and it is the same ordinary constant coefficient ring on both sites. Step 5 puts $Q$ in $D^+(Z_e,A)$ and step 6 makes $i$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] applies with $u=i$ and $K=Q$: its specified mate $b_{i,Q}:C_TRi_{e,*}Q\to Ri_{p,*}C_ZQ$ is defined and invertible. This is the named morphism in the item, rather than an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism. No step required finite Tor amplitude of $B$ or local freeness of $V^h$. The zero complex can be used for a zero input; on the empty site every term is zero; and none of the inequalities or cited results requires either interval to have positive length.
